entries.claim: The Latin text in this revision of Divinum Officium is used for comparison with the printed Missal.

locator.section: Postcommunio continuing Monday after the first Sunday of the Passion, above the Tuesday heading; Per Dominum nostrum through Deus.

entries.claim: This separate Postcommunion prints the accented conclusion with no comma after Christum and the colon and uppercase Qui after tuum, ending with Deus. The composite uses nostrum through Deus.; the cue words Per eúndem Dóminum come from p. 16, and this page supplies neither the final duration nor Amen.

locator.section: Top conclusion and response before the Nativity preface dialogue; Per omnia saecula saeculorum. R. Amen.

entries.claim: The top chant line prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen. The composite joins musical syllable divisions and omits the response marker. Only these five words are used; the Nativity preface dialogue and body are excluded.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a; Father-addressed oration conclusion

entries.claim: RG 115 a supplies the full Father-addressed conclusion, ending with Amen. It controls the expansion rule, not the selected composite transcript's accents or its accidental seams.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 b; mention of the Son at the beginning of an oration

entries.claim: RG 115 b prescribes Per eundem Dominum nostrum, etc. ut supra when an oration addressed to the Father mentions the Son at its beginning. This Postcommunion names the Son in its opening clause (unigéniti Fílii tui recensíta nativitáte), and its printed cue instantiates the rule. The end-mention rule in 115 c is not used here.

locator.section: Rubricae generales Missalis romani, nn. 505, 511 i, 513 a, 514.

entries.claim: The celebrant says or sings the postcommunion and its conclusion.

locator.section: Proper body and abbreviated conclusion cue; full ending supplied from the printed formulae on pp. 123 and 226 under RG 115 a–b

entries.claim: This proper-page locus supplies the body and the abbreviated conclusion cue, not the expanded ending.
